Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M), led by deep-tech investors Plural (whose portfolio spans fusion energy and space exploration), Relay is scaling faster than 99.98% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen
Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.
THE TEAM
• ~110 people, more than half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation
Overview
Relay is a parcel delivery network. Every night, parcels from online retailers arrive at our sort centres, are sorted into delivery routes, and go out the next day with couriers. Two things have to go right for that to work.
Routing is the planning side: software that decides, before parcels have even arrived, which ones to expect, how to group them into routes, and how to make those routes efficient for couriers to drive. Sortation is the physical side: warehouse teams and sorting robots turning a building full of parcels into neatly separated routes, thousands of times a night.
The two are tightly coupled. If the plan expects a parcel that never arrives, a courier's route has a hole in it. If the warehouse sorts a parcel the plan didn't expect, it has nowhere to go. This role owns the analytics across both: spotting when either side is off, working out why, and building the case for what to change.
Your work splits between a daily operational rhythm (is the network healthy this morning, and if not, why) and deeper investigations (what is driving cost, where is the plan falling short of what's possible, what should we change). Your analysis won't sit in a dashboard waiting to be discovered - it will change which parcels get planned for, how warehouse shifts are scheduled, and where the operation focuses its improvement efforts.
Relay operates a centralised data team of around 30 data engineers, analysts, and data scientists, with analysts embedded into teams across the business. You will sit with the Routing & Sortation teams but report into the central data team, working daily with software engineers, warehouse operations, commercial, and finance.
What You'll Do
Routing Monitor the health of each night's route plans: how many parcels each route carries (planned vs what actually happened), how far couriers travel before their first delivery, and the routes no courier should ever be handed - a single parcel stranded miles from every other stop, or one route torn between two towns - and diagnose the cause when any of it moves
Track how well we predict which parcels will arrive each night: when expected parcels don't show up, or unexpected ones do, work out whether the cause was the retailer's data, a warehouse error, or timing, and improve the prediction rules client by client
Act on what you find: flag issues to warehouse managers and retailer-facing teams, and correct the plan when a retailer's parcels arrive outside the normal flow
Monitor the route optimisation engine itself and flag regressions when the software or its inputs change
Quantify how route design affects courier productivity: deliveries per hour, stops per route, distance between drops - and how far our actual routes sit from the best theoretically possible
Build the reporting that diagnoses the middle leg of the network: the van journeys that move sorted parcels from sort centres out to local pick-up points where couriers collect them
Partner with the engineers who build the routing systems to test and validate changes
Sortation Investigate cost per parcel: where are we spending too much, where are savings available, and what's driving the variance
Track warehouse operative performance: throughput, accuracy, shift utilisation, and the balance between permanent and agency labour
Monitor sorting robot efficiency and capacity: what volumes can they sustain, where are the bottlenecks, how do they compare to manual sorting
Build models to predict how many operatives each shift needs, and help automate workforce planning around the best performers
Compare the parcel volumes retailers actually send us against what they told us to expect, and find where the gaps come from
Define KPIs and build dashboards that make routing and sortation performance transparent to operations and leadership
Work with commercial teams to set volume limits and delivery timings that balance growth with operational stability
Who Will Thrive in This Role?
You want to understand how an operation actually works, not just analyse it from a distance
You're comfortable being the person operations and engineering ping first when something looks off in the morning, and you enjoy the detective work of finding out why
You're excited by cost and efficiency problems - finding where money or time is leaking and building the case for how to fix it
You can navigate messy operational data and turn it into metrics people trust
You know how to take a large amount of complex data and visualise it in a way people can actually digest - your dashboards tell someone what to look at and why, rather than presenting every number you have
You're comfortable working with operations teams and embedding your analysis into their daily workflows
You're fluent in SQL and experienced with BI tools, with strong problem-solving instincts
You have at least 3 years experience, ideally with some exposure to logistics or another physical operation
You care about impact, not just insight - you measure success by whether the operation runs better
You communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders and can explain what the data shows and where the limitations are
Fast and Focused Hiring Process
Talent Acquisition Interview - 30mins | Online
Hiring Manager Interview - 45mins SQL Live Coding - 60mins Case Study - 60mins Relay Operating Principles & Impact- 60mins Decision and offer within 48 hours. Our process mirrors our pace of work.
Compensation, Benefits & Workplace
Generous equity, richer than 99% of European startups, with annual top-ups to share Relay’s success.
Private health & dental coverage, so comprehensive you’d need to be a partner at a Magic Circle law firm to match it.
25 days of holidays
Enhanced parental leave.
Hardware of your choice.
Extensive perks (gym subsidies, cycle-to-work, Friday office lunch, covered Uber home and dinner for late nights, and more).
Located in Shoreditch, our office set-up enables the kind of in-person interactions that drive impact. We work 4 days on-site, with 1 day remote.
Who Thrives at Relay?
Aim with Precision: You define problems clearly and measure your impact meticulously.
Play to Win: You chase bold bets, tackle the hard stuff, and view constraints as fuel, not friction.
1% Better Every Day: You believe that small, consistent improvements lead to exponential growth. You move quickly, deliver results, and learn from every experience.
All In, All the Time: You show up and step up. You take ownership from start to finish and do what it takes to deliver when it counts.
People-Powered Greatness: You invest in your teammates. You give and receive feedback with care and candour. You build trust through high standards and shared success.
Grow the Whole Pie: You seek out win-win solutions for merchants, couriers, and our customers, because when they thrive, so do we.
If these resonate, and you combine strong technical fundamentals with entrepreneurial drive, let’s connect.

This is a hands-on, on-the-floor quality role. You'll be the person the lab team comes to. You'll be driving incidents through to closure, following up CAPAs and engineering change orders, keeping the risk register current, and making sure internal and supplier audits actually happen on time. You won't be expected to fix the lab's technical problems yourself — that's the lab team's job — but you will be the one making sure things are investigated properly, documented, actioned and closed.
We work to ISO 15189:2022 and hold UKAS accreditation, so there's real rigour here. There's also a genuine backlog to work through, which means you'll see the impact of your work quickly.
What you'll be doing
* Managing non-conformances end to end — quality issues, security incidents and customer complaints — recording them properly and working with Operations to complete the documentation
* Coordinating root cause investigations and following corrective and preventive actions through to closure
* Driving CAPAs and engineering change orders (ECOs) forward, chasing actions and keeping owners accountable
* Conducting internal and supplier audits, and helping maintain the laboratory audit calendar
* Supporting UKAS accreditation to ISO 15189:2022 — collating evidence, closing non-conformities and verifying changes were implemented effectively
* Maintaining and improving laboratory SOPs and quality documentation
* Maintaining the quality risk register and supporting risk reviews with stakeholders
* Bringing visibility to lab quality actions — for example, visual management in the lab so open actions are seen and closed, not lost in a system
* Compiling monthly error log reports and trend analysis for KPI reviews
* Monitoring EQA and UK NEQAS scheme participation and performance
* Supporting change in the lab so it happens the right way round — SOP updated, training and competency completed, records in place — rather than the team playing catch-up afterwards
* Supporting training and competency so lab staff understand their own role in quality and compliance
About you
Essential
* Solid quality assurance experience in a regulated environment — ISO 15189 or ISO 13485
* Experience in diagnostics or healthcare (rather than pharmaceutical manufacturing)
* Practical, day-to-day experience of incidents, CAPAs, change control and audits
* Internal auditing experience
* Strong follow-through — you're comfortable chasing people, holding owners to deadlines and keeping things moving without being the bottleneck
* Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively as part of a team
* Good written and spoken English
Nice to have
* Bachelor's degree in Biomedical Science, life sciences, engineering or similar
* Knowledge or experience of histopathology and/or digital pathology
* Familiarity with quality systems such as Qualio or Greenlight Guru
* Six Sigma or other process improvement certification
* Experience with generative AI tools and technology
If you have strong quality experience but not a histopathology background, we'd still like to hear from you. The quality fundamentals matter most.

* Experience managing projects and working with multiple stakeholders in an international environment.

* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret technical and business data.
* Confident communicator with excellent written and verbal English skills.

**Response Operations**
* Execute crisis response actions within established SLAs, including activating traveler communication workflows, updating flex waiver policies, and coordinating with airline and hotel partner relations teams.
* Participate in and help facilitate cross-functional war room syncs during active crisis events, driving toward clear actions, owners, and timelines.

* Produce clear, concise performance reports for leadership audiences, translating operational data into narratives that support decisions about resourcing, thresholds, and process improvements.
**Data and Exposure Analysis**
* Query traveler booking, itinerary, and operational data to quantify how many travelers are in an affected area, what products they hold, and what remediation options are available, using SQL across EG's internal data platforms including Trino and Querybook.
* Build and maintain exposure trackers that give leadership a real-time picture of traveler and partner impact during an active event, updated as the situation evolves.
* Translate raw data into clear escalation inputs: how many travelers are affected, what is the financial exposure, what decisions are time-sensitive, and what actions are already in motion.
* Identify patterns across historical crisis events to inform threshold definitions, SLA calibration, and playbook updates.
**AI in Crisis Operations**
Expedia Group is actively investing in AI-assisted operations and expects analysts to be fluent, practical users of AI tools in their day-to-day work. In this role, that means the following.
* Use AI tools to accelerate monitoring and signal detection across large volumes of threat intelligence, news, and meteorological data, reducing the time between event onset and first assessment.
* Leverage AI-assisted drafting to produce first-pass traveler communications, leadership updates, and situation summaries faster, while owning the review, accuracy, and final judgment on every output before it goes out.

**Required**
* 3 to 5 years of professional experience in one or more of the following disciplines: operational meteorology, geopolitical risk analysis, security operations, emergency management, or crisis response.
* Demonstrable ability to assess and communicate complex, fast-moving situations clearly and concisely, in writing and verbally, to both technical and non-technical audiences.
* Experience working in or closely with a 24/7 operations environment, with comfort managing competing priorities under time pressure.
* Strong data skills: comfortable writing and adapting SQL queries, building trackers and dashboards in Excel or Sheets, and translating raw metrics into clear recommendations. The ability to extract signal from operational data quickly is a core part of this job.
* Active use of AI tools in a professional setting, including large language models, AI-assisted monitoring or summarization tools, or automated alerting systems. You do not need to be an AI engineer, but you should be using AI regularly to work faster and better, and be able to speak to how.
* Proficiency with Microsoft 365 suite (Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, Excel), Confluence, and Jira or equivalent ticketing platforms.
* Bachelor's degree in Meteorology, Atmospheric Science, International Relations, Political Science, Security Studies, Geography, Emergency Management, or a closely related field is required. **Preferred**
* Experience with commercial threat intelligence platforms such as Crisis24, NC4, Everbridge, or OSAC, or meteorological data services such as The Weather Company, DTN, or StormGeo.
* Background in travel, hospitality, aviation, or a platform or marketplace business where the customer population is globally distributed and mobile.
* Familiarity with airline disruption frameworks including IRROPs, Event Waivers, and ASCs, or hotel flex policy structures.
* Experience with CRM or case management platforms such as ServiceNow or Salesforce, including hands-on incident or case logging, queue management, and status tracking. Familiarity with managing a case through its full lifecycle from open to close is a meaningful advantage in this role.
* Professional certification in emergency management (CEM, AEM), security (CPP, PSP), or a related discipline.
**What Sets You Apart**
*The best candidates for this role think in systems, not checklists. You understand that a Category 4 storm making landfall in Cancun is not just a weather event. It is a cascade of flight cancellations, hotel evacuations, stranded travelers, partner relations calls, and leadership questions that all hit simultaneously. You have been in that kind of environment before. You know how to stay calm, communicate clearly, and keep others oriented when things are moving fast.*
**How a Strong Analyst Operates at EG**
Crisis operations does not reward hesitation. The value this role delivers comes from the speed and accuracy of judgment under pressure. A strong analyst at EG does the following.
* Recognizes early signals and assesses what requires immediate attention, distinguishing developing situations from background noise before others have flagged them.
* Prioritizes traveler safety, material exposure, and time-sensitive decisions above completeness, because in crisis work a good decision now is almost always better than a perfect decision later.
* Moves from information gathering to recommendation and action quickly, without waiting to be asked what the next step is.
* Escalates early when delay could increase traveler, partner, operational, or reputational impact, and escalates with enough context that the person receiving it can act immediately.
* Maintains momentum across handoffs, approvals, communications, and follow-up, treating every open thread as their responsibility until it is formally closed or handed to a named owner.
* Stays calm and accurate under pressure, because the organization takes its cue from how the analyst communicates, and panic or imprecision in a crisis brief is its own kind of risk.

# Senior Product Manager
Remote, UK
**Type:** Full-time, salaried employment **Location:** Remote, United Kingdom only. **Salary Range:** £90,000 - £105,000 + stock options.
**Who We Are**
Focal Systems is the industry leader in retail AI solutions. We are headquartered in San Francisco, California with operations in Canada and the UK, and a tech-hub in Poland. We are a Deep Learning first company. Our mission is to automate and optimize brick and mortar retail using deep learning computer vision. Focal Systems has been deployed at scale with some of the top retailers in the world.
We seek smart, creative and passionate people who want to help build a great and enduring company and deploy Deep Learning to the world! **What You Will Be Responsible For**
As Senior Product Manager, you will take ownership of how data is processed at Focal, and shape what that path becomes: from the imports that bring a retailer's planograms, inventory and store metadata into our platform, through the pipelines that turn them into signal, to the metrics and reports their head office acts on. You will work with data engineering, data scientists, analytics, customer success and the retailers themselves. What you build are data products, and the measure of one is what a retailer does differently because of it.
This is a hands-on role. You will set direction and priorities as we roll out to hundreds of new stores, but you are also expected to know the systems well enough to be a partner in an engineering design conversation, pull your own numbers when something looks wrong, and hold a strong position in the discussions with customers.
**What We Are Looking For**
* You are a peer to the engineers you work with, someone who understands the systems well enough to know what is expensive and why and when to push back
* You are drawn to the seams between teams, where ownership is shared and the hardest problems live
* You write your own queries and interrogate the answers before anyone else has to, and you can name the business number a data product of yours moved
* You can change your mind in a technical argument, and you can point to the time you did
* You have strong judgment about what not to build, and you have killed your own work when it stopped earning its place
* You use AI as part of how you actually work, and you have built things with it that other people went on to use, not demos you gave once
* You communicate complicated things crisply to people who do not share your context, including customers hearing an answer they did not want
* You build things that outlast you, whether runbooks, tooling or documented decisions, because you would rather remove yourself as a dependency than be indispensable
**What You Will Do**
* Own product direction for the full data path, from how a retailer's data arrives to what our reports say, and set the priorities where the two ends pull against each other
* Own how customer data gets into Focal: imports, planograms, store metadata, cut-off configuration, and the chain-specific flows each retailer needs
* Own what comes out and whether anyone acts on it: the metrics, the reporting APIs, the insight-generating agents, and the customer-facing dashboards a head office runs its week on
* Run discovery with retailers and store colleagues, and turn what you learn into a product
* Ship, then find out whether anyone used it, and act on the answer
* Automate your own work with AI and share what you build with the rest of the product team
**What You Need to Be Successful**
* 5+ years in product management, including real time on a technically deep product where you owned integrations, data, or both
* Enough technical depth to reason about APIs, data pipelines and system boundaries, and to be an equal partner in an engineering discussion
* Experience building for a hierarchy of users who need different things from the same data: a store manager, a regional director and a head of supply chain reading one dataset three ways, served by one configurable surface
* Hands-on comfort with SQL and the ability to answer your own data questions
* Fluency in the analytics and BI tooling landscape, and a view on what makes a dashboard worth returning to rather than merely correct
* Demonstrated ownership of a product roadmap end to end, from problem definition through to something shipped and adopted
* A track record of getting things done across teams, and the communication to influence engineering and commercial partners
* Experience working directly with enterprise customers, including holding a position they disagree with
* Comfortable operating remote-first, across a distributed team
* Willingness to travel occasionally for store and customer visits
**What Would Set You Apart**
* Experience in working with high-volume, noisy sensor or computer-vision data
* Experience with change data capture into a cloud warehouse (ideally Snowflake)
* Experience shipping AI-powered features, including the call on when a model is good enough to ship
**Why Focal Systems**
Joining Focal Systems means becoming part of a company that's truly making a difference in the retail world. Here's why you should consider us:
* **Strong Values and Mission:** We are a tightly-knit team with an ambitious mission and a strong set of core values, which define our approach to business and have successfully guided us since inception.
* **Exceptional Team:** We are a team of hard-working, fun-loving professionals from some of the most eminent universities, research labs, and tech companies of our time. We pride ourselves on recruiting exceptional individuals to help us redefine the state-of-the-art.
* **Outstanding Partners:**We work with 10+ of the largest retailers in the world and have a world-class roster of investors, advisors and partners to support & advise us in our endeavours.
**What we offer**
We care deeply about the health, happiness, and wellbeing of all of our employees. We offer:
* Competitive Salary & Attractive Stock

# Chair of Access Review Committee (ARC)
United Kingdom
Apply now
## Company Description
Genomics England is a global leader in enabling genomic medicine and research, focused on creating a world where everyone benefits from genomic healthcare. Building on the 100,000 Genomes Project, we support the NHS’s world-first national whole genome sequencing service and run the growing National Genomic Research Library, alongside delivering numerous major genomics initiatives. By connecting research and clinical care at national scale, we enable immediate healthcare benefits and advances for the future.
Our mission is to provide the evidence and digital systems so that by 2035 genomics could play a role in up to half of all healthcare interactions, whilst securing the UK’s position as the best place to discover, prove and benefit from genomic innovations.
We are accelerating our impact and working with patients, doctors, scientists, government and industry to improve genomic testing, and help researchers access the health data and technology they need to make new medical discoveries and create more effective, targeted medicines for everybody.
Behind the Healthcare and Research outcomes, Genomics England delivers through designing, developing and operating complex healthcare software systems.
We're on the cusp of big changes with the real prospect of genomics becoming the fabric of everyday healthcare through the lifetime – from birth to old age.
## Job Description
The ARC Chair will take an engaged role in:
* Effectively fulfilling the remit of the ARC, demonstrating appropriate decisions are being given to data access requests (in line with Genomics England’s generic NHS REC approval) while ensuring the process is robust and streamlined.
* Work with the Committee Manager, the Research Management team and the Ethics team to agree agendas for Committee meetings, supporting the preparation of pre-read documents, reviewing minutes.
* Ensure ARC members are able to deliver on the requirements of their membership, managing (actual or perceived) conflicts of interest of members, asking members to recuse themselves as needed, and escalating any concerns to the Committee Manager as required.
* Ensuring appropriate representation at ARC meetings, that quorum is met for decision-making, and engaging with the committee manager as and when new members need to be recruited.
* Identifying and leading discussion on emerging issues of data governance and access in relation to the management and security of the Genomics England Research Environment.
* Ensuring continuous improvement of the structure and operations of ARC to support the expansion of the NGRL and Genomics England’s research endeavors.
**Specific responsibilities for the Chair**
Alongside key working relationships at Genomics England (Chief Ethics & Engagement Officer, Committee Manager, Director of Ethics, Director of Scientific Impact & Partnerships (SIP), the Research Management team), The ARC Chair will:
* Lead on steering and reviewing the progress and success of the ARC, including leading on:
+ Refreshing the ARC model and strategy
+ Developing and chairing an effective system for reviewing and monitoring data access approvals and appropriate use of NGRL data
* Ensuring effective ways of working, communication and approval pathways for ARC members
* Act to consider the interests of Genomics England’s communities, including participants/patients providing data to the NGRL; the general public (given the publicly funded nature of Genomics England); employees, scientists and clinicians engaged in genomic research or clinical care; medical charities; and other potential collaborators.
* Ensure rules, policies and procedures relevant to the work of the ARC are adhered to where applicable (e.g., Genomics England’s Data Release Policy, Airlock policy)
* Support development and review of Genomics England policies relating to data ethics and information governance, particularly where relevant to the NGRL.
* Chair the ARC meetings according to ARC’s Terms of Reference; and engage with other Genomics England committees as required, most notably the Science Advisory Committee (SAC), the Participant Panel, the Ethics Advisory Committee (EAC), the Airlock Committee and the Ethics & Data Protection Group (EDPG).
* Support and promote active involvement of ARC members from the Participant Panel in the ARC’s discussion and decision-making.
* Champion equality and diversity in decision-making, and ensure ARC members and potential members, are treated fairly and equally, and their views and opinions considered, regardless of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion/belief or age.
## Qualifications
**Essential**
* Extensive senior-level experience of discovery and/or translational patient focussed research, with a UK academic, NHS or industry background, and/or experience from a sector with extensive data governance experience
* A strong track record of working with research participants, clinicians, and academic and commercial researchers
* Experience of and passion for including participants and patients in your work and in decision- making processes
* Previous experience of Chairing and leading boards, committees or working groups
* Strong leadership, communication and diplomatic skills
* Ability to work with discretion, impartiality and fairness
* Strategic and forward thinking, able to address challenges, provide innovative and well considered advice, and follow through on necessary actions
* Based primarily in the UK
**Desirable**
* Familiarity and experience working on areas relevant to the remit of the ARC. For example, data governance and access, discovery research using genomic data, Secure Data Environments, high-performance compute usage and equity and diversity in research
* Knowledge of industry/academic partnerships and knowledge transfer
* Understanding of the importance of various forms of research activities and outputs in the UK genomics ecosystem
## Additional Information
**For more information including the foreword from Dr Natalie Banner, our Chief Ethics and Engagement Officer (CEEO) please click to open: Access Review Committee Chair candidate briefing pack**
**Appointment/terms**
* The role is expected to report into the Genomics England Board via the Chief Ethics & Engagement Officer (CEEO). The role holder is expected to work within the Research Ethics Committee (REC) conditions of approval, and the expectations set by the Executive Leadership Team (in particular the CEO and CEEO).
**Term of appointment**
The appointment shall be for 3 years, with a performance review at the end of each year. The term of appointment is renewable for one further term of 3 years, with annual reviews/check-ins.
**Time commitment and support available**
* The time commitment for the role is expected to be around 16-19 days per annum
* Preparation ahead of ARC meetings (expected to be minimum 4 per year), including agenda reviews, reading pre-reads, preparing other ARC members for the meetings and soliciting input and feedback from any and all ARC members
* Monthly 1-hour meetings with ARC Committee Manager and appropriate members of Genomics England.
* Chair’s actions and other out-of-session items and ensuring continuity of ARC business and adequate consideration of agenda items for upcoming meetings
* Genomics England provides secretariat support via the ARC Committee Manager function (preparing pre-reads, providing Genomics England with updates when required, agenda item suggestions and other secretarial support)
* Reviewing of commercial and academic applications through an online portal (currently Jira Service Desk), reviewing comments made on the portal by ARC members and ensuring timely progression of the review process and providing ARC decisions to applicants.
**Remuneration**
This role is remunerated at £7883.00/year (paid monthly). The amount is set according to UK Government guidelines at the equivalent level of a Non-Executive Director and will be discussed upon application. All reasonable expenses that arise from attending face to face meetings will be reimbursed, subject to Genomics England’s expenses policy.

* Strong Java programming skills, ideally in a real-time low latency / zero GC environment.
* High desire to produce organised, readable, and maintainable software.
* Proven problem-solving ability with critical and creative thinking.
* Effective communicator in both written and verbal mediums.
* Hands-on experience writing robust, automated unit and integration test suites to ensure code reliability.
**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
* Prior experience working on an electronic trading platform, including reference data, market data & FIX.
* Ability to balance multiple, time-sensitive projects while maintaining a longer term, strategic focus.
* Knowledge of Kafka, Python, SQL and/or Linux would be beneficial.
* Prior experience of a sequencer/event-based architecture, and/or Zero-GC Java.

In Internal Audit, we ensure that Goldman Sachs maintains effective controls by assessing the reliability of financial reports, monitoring the firm’s compliance with laws and regulations, and advising management on developing smart control solutions. Our group has unique insight on the financial industry and its products and operations. We’re looking for detail-oriented team players who have an interest in financial markets and want to gain insight into the firm’s operations and control processes.
**WHAT WE LOOK FOR**
Goldman Sachs Internal Auditors demonstrate strong risk and control mindsets, analytical, exercise professional skepticism and are able to challenge and discuss effectively with management on risks and control measures. We look for individuals who enjoy learning about audit, businesses and functions, have innovative and creative mindsets to adopt analytical techniques to enhance audit techniques, building relationships and are able to evolve and thrive in teamwork and in a fast-paced global environment.

As the third line of defense, Internal Audit’s mission is to independently assess the firm’s internal control structure, including the firm’s governance processes and controls, and risk management and capital and anti-financial crime frameworks, raise awareness of control risk and monitor the implementation of management’s control measures. In doing so, internal Audit:
• Communicates and reports on the effectiveness of the firm’s governance, risk management and controls that mitigate current and evolving risk
• Raise awareness of control risk
• Assesses the firm’s control culture and conduct risks
• Monitors management’s implementation of control measures
Goldman Sachs Internal Audit comprises individuals from diverse backgrounds including chartered accountants, developers, risk management professionals, cybersecurity professionals, and data scientists. We are organized into global teams comprising business and technology auditors to cover all the firm’s businesses and functions, including securities, investment banking, consumer and investment management, risk management, finance, cyber-security and technology risk, and engineering.

* Assist in every step of an audit, including scoping, planning, fieldwork and reporting
* Execute audit testing and supervise junior team members to ensure audit fieldwork is focused on the right areas and documentation meets high quality standards
* Identify risks, assess mitigating controls, and make recommendations on improving the control environment

# Lead AI Engineer, Game Generation
## About Nanogram
Nanogram is a TikTok-style mobile feed where every item is a short, AI-generated browser game - anyone can make one from a prompt.
## The role
The game-generation pipeline is the product, which makes this the most important hire we're making right now. Every game in the feed comes out of it: a creator's prompt → intent extraction → template matching → model routing → asset retrieval → generation → validation and repair → runtime → play telemetry back into the loop. It's built around a fixed library of ~20 proven core mechanics with hard-constraint specs (every line pass/fail checkable), and a quality score fed by real play data - completion, replay, share/remix.
You'll own that system end to end and be judged on two numbers moving at once: playability pass rate up, cost per generation down, at volume.
This is not a prompt-engineering role, and not a research role where someone else ships your work. It's also not "LLM app" building - the output here has to compile, run and be fun, millions of times, at a cost that works. You'll work with core engineering in Sofia and with game design; there's a team on the pipeline today and you become its technical owner, and lead it if you can. Comp is open - we'll pay top of market for the right person.
## What you'll do
* Own the full generation pipeline: intent extraction, template matching, model routing, asset retrieval, generation, validation and repair, runtime, and play telemetry feeding back into the loop.
* Move playability pass rate up and cost per generation down, at volume.
* Run benchmark suites, LLM-as-judge and playability pass/fail checks, and show output quality improving over time.
* Own the economics: tiered model routing, RAG/templates, caching, small-model distillation.
* Stay hands-on in the runtime: browser/JS games, procedural content, asset/image generation.

* Know the economics cold: tiered model routing, RAG/templates, caching, small-model distillation - have cut cost per generation 10x somewhere.
* Strong enough engineer to live in the runtime too: Three.js, Phaser, Babylon, voxel engines, procedural content, asset/image generation.

# Product Growth Manager
## About Nanogram
Nanogram is a TikTok-style mobile feed where every item is a short, AI-generated browser game - anyone can make one from a prompt. We're growing fast and building the product and team in London.
## The role
You'll own the loops inside the app. Nanogram grows when a viewer becomes a creator, a creator publishes again, and a published game brings in new players - you own all three edges. That means the creator side (creation funnel, first-publish activation, draft nudges, XP and levelling, seasonal rewards), the viral side (share, remix, invite, like → follow → push), and the experimentation machine that decides which of it actually works.
A first set of these loops is already designed. The job is to take them from shipped to measured, iterated and compounding - and to find the ones we haven't built yet. Users who publish more than once retain at several times the rate of an average user; the whole role is getting more people across that line and making them bring others.
This is not a marketing role (paid acquisition and creative are separate hires) and not a data engineering role (you read the data, you don't build the pipes). It's also not a generalist PM role - the remit is loops and the numbers behind them, and you'll be judged on weekly active creators and k-factor, not on features shipped. Headquartered in New York, Guggenheim offers a premier investment banking advisory practice to clients from offices across New York, London, Chicago, Boston, Atlanta, and Houston.

You will have meaningful exposure to senior bankers and client representatives as well as the ability to create meaningful relationships with junior bankers.
Candidates should be top performers who are willing to work hard in an unstructured environment where initiative, creativity, maturity and enthusiasm for learning are highly valued. An excitement to join a fast-growing, dynamic, and entrepreneurial team is a plus.

* Support deal teams in developing, maintaining and using financial models
* Perform financial and valuation analysis such as discounted cash flow analysis, multiple valuation analysis
* Perform company and industry research and gain in-depth understanding of sector trends, client challenges and strategies in order to develop innovative and creative solutions for our clients
* Prepare and participate in client presentations and transaction execution
* Interact with senior bankers, clients, lawyers and accountants
* Develop an in depth understanding of Investment Banking product and services: Debt, Equity, Mergers and Acquisitions and Restructuring

* Excellent analytical skills and attention to detail.
* Strong interest for problem solving and client service
* Resourcefulness, intellectual curiosity, enthusiasm and a genuine interest in finance
* Significant level of maturity and the ability to work under pressure as a part of a small team with top company executives and senior management
* Highly organized, with the initiative and ability to multitask and work with limited supervision as a member of a team
* Strong written and oral communication skills
* Working knowledge of MS Excel, MS Powerpoint and MS Word
* Understanding of financial valuation is a plus

# Senior Credit Analyst
London, England, United Kingdom
**Overview:**
The Insights product is an offering for Guidepoint's Institutional investment and corporate clients, that offers teleconferences, surveys, and in-person events. The teleconferences live in a transcript library portal, which covers a wide of industries/topics that enables our clients to make informed decisions. All content features experts from Guidepoint’s proprietary global network and is conceptualized and hosted by former investment professionals (i.e. private equity/hedge fund), sell-side equity research analysts, and industry professionals.
**All applicants must have the right to work in the UK.**
**What You'll Do:**
* Monitor single name corporate credit situations in European markets including new issues, distressed, restructuring/re-orgs, and price dislocations in both leveraged loan and high yield markets. Create original, sell-side type content on these topics
* Conduct bottoms-up company research including reviewing earnings releases, reading investor presentations and analyzing regulatory filings
* Moderate teleconferences on timely topics featuring an expert from Guidepoint’s network with the goal of producing actionable insights for buy-side clients
* Generate ideas and follow key investor views among relevant strategies within European credit
* Can be an in-person position or a fully remote work-from-home position
**What You Have:**
* Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree
* 7 years or more of sell-side or buy-side analyst experience
* Follow a bottoms-up, fundamental approach to investment research focusing on individual companies
* Has prior experience covering single name corporate credit across both bank loan and high yield markets with a European focus; must be proficient in corporate credit analysis, with an emphasis on either loan / High Yield or Distressed strategies
* Ability to work in a fast-paced entrepreneurial environment
* Outgoing personality with the ability to speak with people at all professional levels
* Intellectual curiosity and desire to learn
* Effective time management and organizational skills
* Demonstrated ability to work both individually and as part of a team
**What We Offer:**
* Competitive salary, bonus and benefits
* Excellent medical coverage through BUPA
* Excellent professional development opportunities
* Supportive culture that celebrates and rewards success
* Monthly Happy Hour, Social Events, Summer Fridays
* Year-round company sponsored sports and team building events
* Informal work environment
* Employee Assistance Programs
* Volunteer days
**About Guidepoint****:** Guidepoint powers end-to-end research workflows for the world’s best research teams.
Backed by a global network of more than **2 million experts and over 1,600 employees,** Guidepoint delivers real-time access to expertise, primary research, and actionable knowledge that help organizations make informed decisions. Through consultations, surveys, events, proprietary content, and AI-enabled tools, we support every stage of the decision-making process—from developing hypotheses and gathering insights to validating assumptions and building conviction for critical decisions.
At Guidepoint, our success relies on the diversity of our employees, experts, and clients, which enables us to foster meaningful connections and a broad range of perspectives. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming environment where individuals of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences can contribute and succeed.

The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.
Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its 2025 Design Award winner for Inclusivity. Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.
Overview
We're looking to hire for our Data side of our AI team at Speechify. This role is responsible for all aspects of data collection to support our model training operations. We are able to build high-quality datasets at petabyte-scale and low cost through a tight integration of infrastructure, engineering, and research work. We are looking for a skilled Software Engineer to join us.
What You’ll Do
Be scrappy to find new sources of audio data and bring it into our ingestion pipeline
Operate and extend the cloud infrastructure for our ingestion pipeline, currently running on GCP and managed with Terraform.
Collaborate closely with our Scientists to shift the cost/throughput/quality frontier, delivering richer data at bigger scale and lower cost to power our next-generation models.
Collaborate with others on the AI Team and Speechify Leadership to craft the AI Team’s dataset roadmap to power Speechify’s next-generation consumer and enterprise products.
An Ideal Candidate Should Have
BS/MS/PhD in Computer Science or a related field.
5+ years of industry experience in software development.
Proficiency with bash/Python scripting in Linux environments
Proficiency in Docker and Infrastructure-as-Code concepts and professional experience with at least one major Cloud Provider (we use GCP)
Experience with web crawlers, large-scale data processing workflows is a plus
Ability to handle multiple tasks and adapt to changing priorities.
Strong communication skills, both written and verbal.
What we offer
A fast-growing environment where you can help shape the company and product.
An entrepreneurial-minded team that supports risk, intuition, and hustle.
A hands-off management approach so you can focus and do your best work.
An opportunity to make a big impact in a transformative industry.
Competitive salaries, a friendly and laid-back atmosphere, and a commitment to building a great asynchronous culture.
Opportunity to work on a life-changing product that millions of people use.
Build products that directly impact and support people with learning differences like dyslexia, ADD, low vision, concussions, autism, and more.
Work in one of the fastest-growing sectors of tech, the intersection of artificial intelligence and audio.

Handelsbanken is a relationship bank built on trust, long-term thinking and local decision-making. We provide bespoke banking and wealth management services to personal and corporate customers,
Our decentralised model means decisions are made close to the customer, in our branches. Our central Functions teams play a vital role in supporting the branch network, providing the expertise, governance and infrastructure that enable branches to serve customers effectively and sustainably.

The Operational Risk Manager works within an experienced risk management team which is responsible for providing high quality analysis, advice, guidance and assurance on the management of operational risk to ensure the business complies with relevant policies, frameworks and regulatory expectations. The team is responsible for the development and implementation of the Non-Financial Risk Management Framework (NFRF) and associated processes and tools. They are responsible for overseeing, reviewing and challenging risk assessments / risk management activities as well as promoting consistency and best practice in the application of the NFRF across the Bank. They are also responsible for undertaking control assurance, which is key in helping the business to understand its inherent exposure to risk and overall effectiveness of the control environment. Recommended Provider status, and rapid growth to become the UK's second-largest ski operator. So we're chuffed to bits to be shortlisted for 'Best Customer Centric Culture' at the UK Customer Experience Awards 2026.
Looking to the future, we have huge ambitions for growth. We have grown year on year since 2018 and expect 2026/27 to be our biggest yet. We took 65,000 passengers away to the mountains in winter 2025/26, we came 63rd in the Times top 100 fastest growing UK companies, and we've secured £5.6 million Series A investment. Key to our future success is growing the Heidi team with even more brilliant people than we have now. So we are looking for someone who will be fundamental to the success of our vision and is excited to help us drive that forward.
## The Role
We're looking for a Customer Support Manager who can own the customer experience from the moment someone books to the moment they're home. At Heidi, the customer is everyone's responsibility, and this role holds the standard for what that looks like in practice.
You'll lead around 25 people across four teams, including our UK support function and a remote "follow the sun" operation based in Far East Asia and the Americas that runs for six months of the year. You'll also own our specialist disruption response for when the mountains misbehave.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role, and a rare mix of leadership, judgement and execution. It's an office-based role, and you'll need to be able to work from our office in central Bristol with availability to work some weekends and bank holidays throughout the season.

* ****Customer experience outcomes, post-booking to home**** — own the experience from booking through on-trip to post-trip, across every channel (phone, WhatsApp, email and live chat). Be the single owner of "are our customers getting the experience we promised them".
* ****Own the Duty Manager function -**** including building and managing the Duty Manager rota, ensuring appropriate cover at all times, and personally stepping in to cover Duty Manager shifts when required.
* ****A global, follow-the-sun operation**** — lead four teams totalling ~25 people, including a UK team and remote colleagues covering Far East Asia and the Americas for the six-month season. Own the staffing plans, coverage model, time-zone handovers and seasonal ramp that make genuine 24/7 support real.
* ****Team operating model and accountability**** — scale a structured team with clear reporting lines, ownership and escalation paths. Set development plans, be a calm and decisive point of escalation, and hold a high bar for managerial standards and professionalism across team leads and frontline advisors alike.
* ****Seasonal readiness**** — own operational readiness ahead of each season: staffing, training, tooling, policies and disruption planning, so the team is match-fit before volume peaks.
* ****Onboarding and continuous training**** — run onboarding and ongoing training with measurable knowledge validation and performance tracking, keeping the bar high as the team scales seasonally.
* ****High-stakes decisions and disruption**** — own decision-making in sensitive, high-cost customer cases where there's financial exposure, precedent or reputational risk, and lead the disruption response when weather, roads or suppliers throw something unexpected at us.
* ****Cross-functional alignment**** — work closely with Operations, Product, Retention and Leadership to resolve customer issues, whether they stem from suppliers and fulfilment or anywhere else in the journey. Keep the customer front and centre in decision-making across the business, so every team is pulling in the same direction to raise the customer experience.
* ****Systems, tooling and automation**** — be the champion of the CS tech stack (ticketing, workflows, reporting), working with our Product team to make sure the team has the right tools and systems in place. Drive scalable process improvement, using these tools and AI to reduce friction, prevent recurring issues and improve the experience customers actually have.
* ****Metrics that matter**** — own and improve the measures customers feel: CSAT, response and resolution times, complaint resolution and NPS. You're also accountable for the productivity of the function, such as tickets per agent, and you'll work with our Holiday Experience tech squad to bring down tickets per booking.

* You're a key member of our cross-functional NPS squad, which meets regularly whether NPS is rising or falling, and you help turn customer feedback into product features that positively impact the customer experience.
* The follow-the-sun operation runs reliably across time zones, with clean handovers and genuine overnight coverage.
* Your team knows what they're accountable for and what a great job looks like, and they're developing under your leadership.
* The support team is close to what customers need next, and you work closely with our Holiday Experience tech squad — the team dedicated to improving the customer experience — to turn what you hear and see into real product improvements.
* Manual, fragile processes are steadily replaced with scalable ones, and you're a driving force behind AI adoption in the team, using it where it genuinely helps customers rather than just to cut cost.
## What we're looking for
* 3+ years in Customer Service / Customer Support leadership in a B2C environment.
* Proven experience managing multi-layer teams, including team leads. Experience of geographically distributed or global coverage across time zones is preferred.
* A strong track record of building structure, accountability and performance systems, not just keeping things running.
* Hands-on experience implementing and scaling CS infrastructure: ticketing platforms, workflows, automation and reporting. Experience with platforms such as Intercom or Zendesk, including implementation and optimisation, is a strong advantage. (CRM sits with our Head of Retention, who you'll work closely with, but familiarity with tools like Salesforce and Customer.io is useful.)
* Experience building or significantly upgrading CS operational foundations: process design, escalation frameworks, QA systems, knowledge bases and SLAs.
* Exceptional judgement in customer-facing decisions involving financial exposure, precedent-setting or reputational risk.

* The ability to lead through pressure, ambiguity and peak-season intensity, with high integrity and professionalism as a trusted senior leader.

* You ski and/or are an outdoorsy person. Genuinely useful, not just a nice-to-have.

job_description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.
Roku is changing how the world watches TV
Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.
From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.
What does the team work on?
Roku is the No. 1 TV streaming platform in the US, Canada and Mexico, with more than 100 million active accounts. Every ad impression across that platform has to be cleared and priced in real time — that is what the Ads Auctions and Marketplace Optimization team does. We build the auction mechanics, the pricing and pacing logic, and the low-latency systems that run them, balancing outcomes for advertisers, publishers, viewers, and Roku on every request. We are growing the team in Cambridge, which is becoming its largest hub, alongside colleagues in Amsterdam, Austin, San Jose, Ukraine and Uruguay — so you would be shaping how the UK side of this team works rather than inheriting it.
What is the role?
You will build the systems that apply mathematical and algorithmic rigour to optimise across multiple objectives, deciding which ads get served, in which placements, and when. The work spans auction mechanics, optimisation, the output of predictive ML models, and the real-time infrastructure underneath, mostly in Java on the JVM. It is hands-on and senior in scope: expect to move between whiteboard-level design and production code in the same week, and to own problems from framing through rollout. You will work directly with the hiring manager and a small group of senior engineers, in codebases shared with other ads engineers, on problems where your decisions are visible in revenue. You will optimise for second-order effects in a marketplace where participants react to each other, and to us, in real time. We are looking for people who are enthusiastic about solving these kinds of problems.
How will I use AI at Roku?
At Roku, we don't just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We're looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they've used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact.
We value your AI skills if you have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. And you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.
What are the responsibilities of the role?
Design and build components of Roku's real-time ad auction and marketplace systems
Own the multi-objective optimisation at the core of the auction, balancing what advertisers, publishers, viewers, and Roku each want from the same impression
Own development work end to end, from framing the problem through production rollout
Build and operate JVM services where latency and reliability are product requirements, not stretch goals
Use probability, statistics and experimentation to test changes before and after launch
Work with AI tooling as a normal part of how you design, build, test and review
Explain technical trade-offs clearly to engineering and cross-functional partners
What experience would help someone be successful in this role at Roku?
Around six or more years building production software, with strong systems judgement
Production experience in Java or another JVM language, or depth in a comparable statically typed language such as C#, C++ or Go, and the appetite to ramp on Java
Comfort designing and operating distributed systems at scale and low latency
A solid grounding in maths, algorithms, probability and statistics as applied to real systems
Demonstrated AI and agentic-tooling fluency, as described above
Ad tech, auctions or marketplace experience is preferred, and we move quickly for candidates who have it
Comparable experience on mathematically rigorous or optimisation-heavy problems in another domain is an acceptable alternative

Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.
What are some of the benefits?
Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.
Accommodations
Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com.
What should I know about Roku's culture?
Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV. We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002. # About the Role
We are looking for a Validation Engineer to sit at the centre of our test and validation operation — someone who can both define what needs to be tested and get on the floor to do it.
This is not a pure execution role. You will work with Test and Validation Engineers and systems owners to understand what a subsystem must demonstrate, then translate that into structured test procedures, acceptance criteria, and measurement plans. When the rig is ready, you run the tests yourself: hooking up sensors, operating DAQ systems, acquiring clean data, and writing the reports that engineering teams sign off on.
Fabrication skills are a bonus — if you can also turn a bracket or jig to support a test setup, that is valuable, but the defining output of this role is structured, repeatable test procedures and the data they produce.
.
# What You'll Do
### **Test Definition & Planning**
* Test Procedures: Author clear, structured test procedures from engineering requirements or verbal briefs — covering setup, instrumentation, execution steps, pass/fail criteria, and data capture format.
* Acceptance Criteria: Work with systems owners and senior engineers to define measurable acceptance criteria for hardware under test.
* Test Plans: Translate validation scope into test plans that sequence activities, flag dependencies, and align with the project schedule.
* Method Development: Identify gaps in existing test coverage and propose new methods or measurement approaches to close them.
### **2. Measurement & Data Acquisition**
* Electromechanical Measurement: Set up and operate measurement equipment for electromechanical testing — sensors, actuators, harnesses, and mechatronic assemblies.
* Mechanical Measurements: Perform mechanical measurements including speed, displacement, force, stress, and strain using appropriate instrumentation (load cells, accelerometers, strain gauges, encoders).
* DAQ Systems: Configure, operate, and maintain Data Acquisition systems. Connect sensors, set up logging sessions, verify signal integrity, and export structured datasets for engineer review.
### **3. Test Execution & Reporting**
* Test Execution: Execute test procedures to the letter — operating rigs, maintaining conditions, logging deviations, and flagging anomalies in real time.
* Engineering Reports: Author clear engineering test reports — data tables, plots, test conditions, pass/fail outcomes, and observations that engineering teams can act on directly.
* Root Cause Analysis: Participate in fault investigation, applying systematic thinking to identify failure modes in hardware under test.
* External Test Houses: Prepare samples and documentation for external test house engagements; liaise on logistics and scheduling.
### **4. Lab Operations & Organisation**
* Tooling & Consumables: Coordinate ordering of tooling, PPE, and consumables — tracking stock levels and ensuring the lab is always equipped to work.
* 5S Management: Contribute to and sustain the 5S regime on the test floor.
* Equipment Health: Perform routine maintenance and calibration checks on lab equipment; flag items requiring service before they become blockers.
### **5. Component Familiarisation & Supplier Interaction**
* Domain Knowledge: Familiarity with components used in robotics, aerospace, or automotive systems — understanding what a part is, how it moves, and what it can tolerate.
* Supplier Liaison: Interact with external suppliers for parts, materials, and services — communicating requirements clearly and following up on lead times.
# What We're Looking For
* Background: Hands-on experience in a test and validation environment in robotics, aerospace, or automotive — you understand how these systems are qualified, not just how they are built.
* Test Definition: Demonstrable experience writing test procedures, test plans, or acceptance criteria from engineering requirements. You have authored methods, not just followed them.

* Measurement & DAQ: Experience with electromechanical test and measurement equipment and at least one DAQ platform (National Instruments, Dewesoft, HBK, or similar) — hardware setup, software configuration, and data export.

* Fabrication: Competency with machine tools (lathe, mill, pillar drill) and hand tools for light fabrication of fixtures and jigs.
* Scripting: Python or MATLAB for test data processing or basic automation.
* Root Cause Analysis: Familiarity with structured RCA techniques (5-Why, Fishbone, FMEA).
* 5S / Lean: Experience running or auditing a 5S programme in a lab or production environment.
* External Test Houses: Prior experience coordinating sample preparation and logistics with accredited test facilities.
## **The Equipment You Will Work With**

* Sensors: Load Cells, Strain Gauges, Accelerometers, Encoders, Thermocouples

## Job Description
**About IFS Copperleaf**
IFS Copperleaf helps the world’s largest asset-intensive organizations — utilities, energy, water, transportation, and more — decide where to invest billions in capital to deliver the most value, using AI-powered decision analytics. Our customers defend and optimize the infrastructure that societies depend on.
**The Role**
As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you sit cross-functionally across the Sales, Product, R&D, and Implementation teams. For our most critical pursuits, you stand up our current product on the customer’s own data, fast, to prove value inside the deal. And when a customer needs something our product does not yet do, you use modern AI tools to rapidly prototype a near-production ready solution and put it in front of them. You turn “we can’t do that” into “here’s how,” and the strongest prototypes go on to shape our roadmap.
You own the technical outcome from discovery through production adoption. Your job is to win deals by delivering fast and with value in the current production environment, prototyping and articulating value from customer requirements, measuring and proving value across customer workflows, and continuously coordinating field-observed customer needs, ideas, roadmaps, and visions with the product and sales organizations. You are the shaper that understands customers’ needs, hypothesizes on value, co-creates the solution, and can test, measure, and validate the outcomes.
**What You Will Do**
* Work alongside Solutions Consultants and Account Executives with our most innovative and strategic accounts as well as our most important net new opportunities.
* Own discovery, technical scoping, architecture, implementation, evaluation, productionization, adoption, and handoff for strategic customer solutions. Deploy and prove value.
* Prototype aggressively; productionize deliberately.
* For sales and product management validation, build the smallest safe prototype that tests the hypothesis inside the deal’s timeline. For production use, engineer for security, reliability, observability, maintainability, and integration with the customer’s architecture.
* Build, deploy, and evaluate with customer data; measure adoption, workflow impact, reliability, and time-to-value; iterate with technical and business stakeholders.
* Partner closely with Product and R&D to turn validated customer patterns and production evidence into supported roadmap investments, reusable components, and platform improvements.
* Turn recurring needs into reusable accelerators so the whole team moves faster.
* Develop solution specifications with the customer to feed product and engineering organizational understanding, continuously updating the specification as the solution and outcomes evolve.
* Work with Product continuously as business value emerges and outcomes become known to evaluate business potential, broader market needs, competitive differentiation aspects, and functional/technical specifications.
**How We Measure This Role**
* Influenced ACV on deals where an FDE engaged.
* Time to first working prototype on the customer’s own data.
* Graduation rate: the share of prototypes that reach production.
* Patterns and accelerators shipped, and how often they get reused on later engagements.
* Recurring gaps taken to Product, and what Product decided.
## Qualifications
**What You Bring**
**Required**
* **Customer-facing and commercial ability.** You can run a technical discovery session, hold a value conversation with both technical and business stakeholders, and connect what you build to the customer's outcome and the deal's value case. The ultimate value of this role is connecting technology to real business outcomes.
* **Abstraction and reuse.** You can generalize what you built for one customer into a reusable accelerator the team applies on the next engagement.
* **AI and agentic engineering.** LLM application development, RAG, prompt and context engineering, and agent orchestration, including the judgment for when to use single versus multi-agent patterns and how to handle memory and state. Modern AI coding tools such as Claude Code as daily practice, not novelty.
* **Familiar with enterprise integrations in a regulated utility market.** You’re familiar with key customer systems such as ESRI ArcGIS/Smallworld, IBM Maximo/EAM, SAP/Oracle ERP/PPM, and PowerBI/reporting systems. Intropic is a financial information and software company operating at the cutting edge of global capital markets. You will keep the day-to-day of Intropic's security and IT running, and build the systems that secure it further. Colleagues rely on the IT you run. Our SOC 2 relies on the evidence you keep clean. Where the work repeats, you build it away.
This role is built for someone with solid IT experience who wants to move into security. You already know how to run an estate: laptops, accounts, SaaS apps, and access paths. Here you'll put that knowledge to work on the security side, because you cannot write a good detection or a useful guardrail without knowing what normal looks like. The role is a mix of IT, security engineering, and GRC, and it is an engineering role throughout. Anything you find yourself doing twice by hand is a candidate for automation, and you will have the tools and the mandate to build it. As you grow, the security engineering side of the role grows with you.

**Security Engineering - 40%**
* Assist in engineering the security of our cloud infrastructure across AWS and GCP, from individual EC2 instances to a large EKS microservice estate.
* Assist in building new detections. Expand coverage where we're blind and cut the noise where we're not.
* Assist in threat modelling new products and services before they ship, and embed security checks directly into CI/CD.
* Assist with incident response, gathering evidence and running containment steps.
* Build tooling that improves how we work, from enrichment scripts to integrations between our security systems.
* Help build the guardrails around our AI agent usage (Claude Code and similar) as we work out what good looks like.

* Run onboarding and offboarding for joiners and leavers, and build the automation that makes both fast and complete.
* Manage our fleet of roughly 100 endpoints through Jamf and Intune (about 90% macOS, 10% Windows): enrolment, patching, configuration profiles, and compliance.
* Be the first responder for colleague IT and access questions, and resolve them quickly and courteously.
* Administer our core SaaS estate, including Google Workspace and GitLab access, and script away the repetitive parts.
**GRC - 20%**
* Keep our SOC 2 evidence current in Drata. Chase down failing monitors and automate evidence collection wherever possible.
* Help prepare for the yearly Type II audit and the annual pentest.
* Maintain security policies and track exceptions.

* Solid professional experience in IT. Desktop support, sysadmin, or endpoint management.
* Hands on experience with Jamf and Git in a professional settings
* Basic scripting ability in Python or Bash
* Comfort with macOS and Windows administration
* Familiarity with how networks, identity, and access control work.
* Experience using AI tools in your own workflow
* A genuine interest in security as a career. We will invest in training you, and we want that investment to land.
* Patience and courtesy with end users. A large part of this job is helping colleagues, and doing it well earns the trust that makes the security work possible.
* High attention to detail. Offboarding done sloppily is a security incident waiting to happen.

* Exposure to Intune.
* Exposure to AWS or any cloud platform.
* Personal projects, a home lab, CTF experience, or security certifications in progress (Security+ or similar).
* Familiarity with SOC 2 or any compliance framework.

Sales and delivery are working well.
